title: Finite-coefficient etale exceptional normalization and its dualizing comparisons
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\geq1$. Use the small pro-etale bounded constructible finite-Tor categories and derived operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and its transported etale compact-support adjunction. All schemes below are finite-type $k$-schemes; their absolute separatedness is not assumed. All morphisms below are separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Write $\omega_h=Rh^!A$, $c_{v,u}:R(vu)^!\simeq Ru^!Rv^!$ for the adjunction conjugate of [thm-sf-comp-composition, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], and use the specified $\theta$ and $\beta$ of [def-pur-co-smoothness]. For composable smooth morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] put $\sigma_{u,v}=c_{v,u,A}^{-1}\theta_{u,\omega_v}\mathrm{sym}$.

For every etale $e:U\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], there is a canonical natural isomorphism $\rho_e:Re^!\simeq Le^*$ on these categories. Its normalization is the unique right-adjoint comparison preserving the sum/evaluation counit after etale transport and the proper-support identification of compact support with the exact etale sum extension [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]. Put $\eta_e=\rho_{e,A}:\omega_e\simeq A_U$, inserting the coefficient-unit pullback comparison. Then:

(1) $\rho_{e,K}\theta_{e,K}$ is the unit constraint $Le^*K\otimes^L\omega_e\xrightarrow{1\otimes\eta_e}Le^*K\otimes^LA_U\simeq Le^*K$.

(2) These comparisons preserve identities and composition: for etale $e:U\to X$, $v:X\to T$,
$$\rho_{ve,K}=Le^*(\rho_{v,K})\circ\rho_{e,Rv^!K}\circ c_{v,e,K},$$
with the canonical derived-pullback composition inserted. For a Cartesian base change of $e$ along any separated finite-type $w:X'\to X$, with $e':U'\to X'$ and $w':U'\to U$, the equality $\eta_{e'}\beta_{e,w}=Lw'^*\eta_e$ holds after the coefficient-unit identifications.

(3) If $h:X\to S$ is smooth, put
$$E_{e,h}=\rho_{e,\omega_h}\circ c_{h,e,A}:\omega_{he}\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*\omega_h.$$
Then $E_{e,h}\sigma_{e,h}$ is the unit constraint $\omega_e\otimes^LLe^*\omega_h\xrightarrow{\eta_e\otimes1}Le^*\omega_h$. For a Cartesian square $R'\xrightarrow{e'}R$, $T'\xrightarrow eT$ with vertical smooth maps $h':R'\to T'$, $h:R\to T$ and etale horizontal maps, the canonical smooth base-change map satisfies
$$\beta_{h,e}=\sigma_{h',e}^{-1}\circ E_{e',h}^{-1}:Le'^*\omega_h\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{h'},$$
where $he'=eh'$ and the target of $\sigma_{h',e}^{-1}$ is identified with $\omega_{h'}$ using $\eta_e$.

All these identities commute with further compatible open restriction. No orientation or Tate twist is chosen.

source.place: Step 1: natural etale normalization, theta the identity and beta canonical; made precise with compact-support composition and sum/evaluation counits

For a separated etale morphism with finite constant coefficients the exceptional inverse image is canonically ordinary pullback preserving adjunction counits and composition
The dualizing complex of an etale morphism is the unit and its canonical projection formula tensor map is identity under the sum extension adjunction
